decision.supported: Repeated provider classification and provider-identity cleanup SQL in catalogue fixture insertion was a material contributor to the measured regression.
notSupported: The experiment does not establish that provider-identity SQL was the only cause of the regression.
The experiment does not establish current-source performance acceptance.
The experiment does not characterize a large Gmail mailbox, provider latency, native responsiveness, or long-duration resource behavior.
decision.requiredNextEvidence: After source and dependencies are frozen, run exactly three fixed repeats at 2,000, 30,000, 100,000 and 200,000 messages against the unchanged historical baseline. Do not reset the baseline or retry adaptively.

historicalBaseline.scope: Historical loopback scripted IMAP and SQLite debug-profile measurement on an Apple M1 Max. It is retained unchanged and was not reset by this investigation.

hostLoad.observation: The accepted causal A/B log recorded one, five and fifteen minute load averages before and after each sample. One-minute values ranged from 346.36 to 390.80.
hostLoad.interpretation: The load was extremely high. Interleaving reduced ordering bias but cannot make this an idle-host acceptance run.

cohortIdentity.warning: The frozen test binaries include dirty performance instrumentation and storage variants and are not identified by Git commit or a complete source-manifest digest. Their binary hashes are the durable cohort identifiers.

pre.behavior: Instrumented pre-optimization implementation with per-row provider classification and per-row non-Gmail identity cleanup.

post.behavior: Instrumented implementation with account-cached provider classification and one account-scoped cleanup for a confirmed non-Gmail account.

dependencyDifferenceFromFinalSource.detail: The A/B binaries predate the later Cargo.lock dependency reconciliation, including the Hickory 0.26.2 family and clipboard-win 5.4.3 updates. The final source also contains later safety refinements for corrupt and mismatched account records, the observation account index, and staged production finalization batching.
dependencyDifferenceFromFinalSource.effect: The A/B comparison is evidence for the bounded storage change, not evidence that the final dependency and source cohort passes performance acceptance.

acceptedCausalExperiment.design: Twelve fixed samples: three repeats for each pre/post and 2,000/30,000 combination, ordered pre then post within each scale and iteration. There were no adaptive retries.

rawLog.portableCopy: All twelve parsed measurements, phase timings, observer timings and load observations are embedded below.

acceptedCausalExperiment.interpretation: The post variant reduced the fixture-insertion median at both measured sizes while the sync median remained close at 2,000 and 30,000 messages. This localizes a material contributor to catalogue fixture insertion. It does not time a large initial production snapshot finalization.

earlyLookupOnlyExperiment.reason: This earlier pass cached provider classification but did not yet replace per-row non-Gmail cleanup with one account-scoped cleanup. Its first 2,000-message pre sample was a 4,529 ms outlier, and host load collection failed because the attempted sysctl call was denied. It is retained separately and was not selected as the final causal A/B.

instrumentation.observer: Each sample records progress-observer call count and total elapsed nanoseconds. Every accepted causal sample made five calls; observed totals were microseconds and do not explain the millisecond-scale difference.
instrumentation.runnerBehavior: Report schema version 2 requires all phases and observer fields, retains failed Rust output, records subprocess wall time and load averages, and fails closed on malformed evidence.

implemented: Catalogue batches cache provider classification per account and perform one account cleanup only for a confirmed non-Gmail account.
The staged UIDVALIDITY replacement finalization path resolves provider classification once and uses the same bounded cleanup behavior.
Missing, invalid JSON, and valid JSON with a mismatched embedded account ID are not treated as confirmed non-Gmail; they retain the legacy touched-locator cleanup.
An account_id index supports observation cleanup without a full-table scan.
productionPathScope.timingLimit: The accepted A/B times catalogue fixture insertion followed by an already-complete no-op sync. The staged production finalization path is covered semantically but does not have a dedicated 30,000-message initial-snapshot timing here.
productionPathScope.gmailLimit: The resilience fixture account is Fastmail. Gmail continues to write identity and observation rows, and the new observation index adds an index write. Large Gmail mailbox performance is uncharacterized.

validation.focusedRust: The listed storage and provider-identity tests passed. The live Gmail identity proof remained ignored and is a skip, not a pass.

restrictedSandboxFullSuite.detail: The restricted sandbox run reported widespread loopback, TLS and network-heavy failures and was interrupted before completion. It was not an isolated normal source-gate environment and is neither passing evidence nor a product-regression conclusion. The main full source gates must run in their established environment.

limitations: The source and dependency cohort differs from both the historical baseline and final current source.
The accepted A/B host was under extreme concurrent load.
Only 2,000 and 30,000 messages were measured; 100,000 and 200,000 remain unmeasured for this change.
The A/B isolates a fixture-insertion contributor but does not prove the entire production sync regression is resolved.
No large Gmail mailbox, native WebKit responsiveness, provider latency, or sustained resource soak was measured.
Temporary binary and raw-log paths are recorded for provenance, but this checked-in document embeds the portable parsed evidence because temporary artifacts can disappear.
